notes: pipeline/BRIEF.md currently describes the ux-agent manual-v3 UI cycle (out of scope for the catalog, main game code out of scope per that brief too), so it is not the brief I am answering. I answered the validation summary given directly in this session's task instead: verdict PASS WITH DRIFT, worst deviations Day 3 measured 61.5% vs target 67% (-5.5%), Day 5 measured 61.5% vs target 56% (+5.5%), Finale measured 39.5% vs target 35% (+4.5%). IMPORTANT: I read pipeline/validation/report.md in full and these numbers do not appear anywhere in it; see the report-missing-latest-entry suggestion below. All four items are retunes of EXISTING augment ids, chosen because they map cleanly onto the kitted-profile harness's day-gated schedule (kernel-panic-site/app/src/game/dev/kitted-profile.ts: hotBoot online day 2, longArms online day 4, one mode-matched pair boost online day 6), so I can say with precision which measured day band each lever touches. No new augment added; pool stays at 18 (4 config, 14 boost).

items.name: LONG ARMS
items.desc: Rotate open junctions up to 3 steps from your built ground instead of 2, and place patch pieces just as far. Bigger setups, bigger cascades.
items.synergy: Cascade setups: extra reach exposes more open junctions before the fold, feeding cascadeRam's 3+/6+/10+ tiers, and lets patch cells bridge slag farther out from built ground.
items.counter: Rotation stays unidirectional (rotCostFor searches forward only), so an enemy REDIRECT into reach-extended territory still costs the full per-elbow undo tax. A smaller radius means fewer nodes sit exposed to that tax at once, so overreach still bleeds RAM, just less of it.
items.engineNote: existing, numeric retune only. duel-power.ts:332 currently returns BASE_REACH + 2 (reach 4) when the kit holds longArms; change to BASE_REACH + 1 (reach 3). longArms comes online at day 4 in the kitted harness (dev/kitted-profile.ts BOOST_SCHEDULE), so it is live for the Day 5 measurement (61.5% vs target 56%, the report's second-worst deviation) and every day after. Trimming the radius by one step is the smallest lever that still leaves it a real upgrade over the base BASE_REACH of 2.

items.name: JAM ANCHOR
items.desc: Your REDIRECT also freezes the junction it twists through the reply. Nothing rotates or redirects it back while it holds.
items.synergy: REDIRECT already has no reach limit, so jamAnchor lets you plant the frozen twist anywhere on the enemy board, denying exactly the junction their fold needs next.
items.counter: A SURGE-tier cascade (6+ lit, surgeTierOf) on the frozen junction's own board shatters every enemy lock, including jamAnchor's freeze: duel-actions.ts:196-202 checks lockedThroughRound and lockedBy generically, not by mode. A big fold beats the freeze outright, same as it beats a CLAMP DRIVER lock.
items.engineNote: existing, numeric retune only. duel-actions.ts:473 currently sets lockedThroughRound to Math.max(current, s.round + 1), which holds the freeze through the reply AND the caster's own next turn, on top of a REDIRECT that already costs nothing extra to cast. Change to Math.max(current, s.round), dropping the caster's-own-next-turn leg so the freeze covers only the immediate reply. This boost comes online day 6 in the kitted harness's mode-pair schedule and is live at Finale (measured 39.5% vs target 35%, +4.5%), where it currently reads as a free REDIRECT-plus-LOCK for 1 RAM.

items.name: TRIPWIRE
items.desc: Your halt traps also burn 2 RAM off the victim's next active turn.
items.synergy: Stacks on cfgArmHalt's full-turn loss for a second punish on the same spring, rewarding a halt-plus-lock DEFEND pairing that can afford to wait for a trap to fire.
items.counter: PURGE disarms the trap before it ever springs, and a trap must be revealed by SCAN first, so a SCAN-tier-2-plus opponent (or tapLine) sees it coming and routes around the whole combo, tripwire included.
items.engineNote: existing, numeric retune only. duel-actions.ts:498 currently sets drain = 3 for a tripwire-boosted halt trap, added on top of a base halt effect that already costs the victim their whole turn. Change to drain = 2. Comes online the same day-6 mode-pair slot as jamAnchor above, so it shares responsibility for the Finale +4.5% overshoot; trimming both keeps the fix spread across the triangle instead of gutting one archetype.

items.name: SIPHON DRIVER
items.desc: ATTACK config: plant siphon traps. A sprung trap drains RAM from its next turn into yours, more at higher ATTACK tiers, and more again when you are the one springing it.
items.synergy: Pairs with echoTap (RAM back on your own next turn whenever one of your traps fires) and siphonPlus for a RAM-positive dive once a couple of traps have sprung.
items.counter: PURGE removes the trap before it ever fires, and it must be revealed (SCAN) first, so a scan-forward opponent denies the whole line the same way they deny halt traps.
items.engineNote: existing, numeric retune only, and scoped narrowly on purpose. duel-actions.ts:491-496 computes siphon drain from the shared SIPHON_STEAL table (2/3/4 by tier, read by tier-3-plus opponents too, per the comment at line 491-492) plus a player-side-only baseline term currently (side === player ? 1 : 0). Change that baseline term to (side === player ? 2 : 0). Do NOT touch SIPHON_STEAL itself, since that table is shared with opponent-side siphon casts and a change there would also buff the machine. Rationale: at Day 3 the kitted harness first randomizes the mode-pair archetype (redirect+purge, armSiphon+purge, armHalt+lock all appear from day 3 on, mixSeed % 3 in kitAtDay), and armSiphon is the weakest of the three pre-boost: armHalt already costs the victim a full turn at base, redirect is free-form with no reach limit, but base armSiphon only drains 2-4 RAM with no boost until siphonPlus (which does not come online in the harness schedule until day 6). That asymmetry is a plausible second driver, alongside arc-side RAM and cell growth, of the Day 3 shortfall (61.5% vs target 67%, the worst deviation in the report). This is a hypothesis from reading the code path, not a simmed confirmation; ask validation to break out Day 3 win rate by mode-pair archetype in the next pass to confirm before trusting this lever alone.

items.idea: dev/kitted-profile.ts's NIGHT_SCHEDULE does not place a DEFEND upgrade pick until index 5 of 9 (day 7), so every dive on days 3 through 6, including the armHalt+lock and armSiphon+purge archetypes that start getting sampled at day 3, runs DEFEND_WIDTH 1 (one purge target, one lock target per cast) the whole time. That is a second plausible contributor to the Day 3 shortfall sitting entirely outside my lane: it is the night upgrade schedule, arc-composer or core-kit territory, not the augment pool.
items.why: If arc-composer or validation wants to test whether the Day 3 dip closes without touching the catalog at all, pulling the first DEFEND pick earlier (trading a later RAM or ATTACK slot) is a cheap thing to try alongside or instead of the cfgArmSiphon retune above, and would isolate which lever actually moved the number.

items.idea: The validation numbers I was told to design against this session (Day 3 measured 61.5% vs target 67%, Day 5 measured 61.5% vs target 56%, Finale measured 39.5% vs target 35%, verdict PASS WITH DRIFT) do not appear anywhere in pipeline/validation/report.md as I read it. The file's newest section is headed '# Cycle ui-integration-2026-07-29' and reports the kit-less curve BIT-IDENTICAL to the deep-balance-2026-07-28 re-baseline on all 11 rows, with no Day 3, Day 5, or Finale percentage table matching 61.5/61.5/39.5 or 67/56/35 anywhere in the file. I grepped for the specific figures and found zero matches.
items.why: My own operating rule is to never design from remembered or unverified numbers, and this repo has already hit exactly this failure mode twice: both deep-balance-2026-07-28 checkpoints in the same report file note 'the agent's Write did not reach this file' and had to be landed by the Orchestrator from a direct harness run instead. I proceeded on the numbers given directly in this session (CLAUDE.md ground truth order ranks the user's current-session word above any doc), but pipeline/validation/report.md needs the real new entry appended, with its harness output and loop-history line, or the next agent to read it will contradict this proposal's premise entirely.
items.disputes: report.md's newest heading, '# Cycle ui-integration-2026-07-29', contains only a kit-less bit-identical table; it has no entry matching the Day 3 / Day 5 / Finale figures cited to me this session.
